name: Grow food in containers
blurb: No garden required — a balcony, a doorstep or a windowsill will grow real food. Container growing has its own rules, mostly about water and pot size.
gear: The biggest pots you can accommodate
A watering can and liquid feed
steps: Choose crops suited to pots: salad leaves, radish, chard, bush beans, chillies, herbs and potatoes in sacks.
Go bigger on pots than feels necessary. Small pots dry out within hours in summer and limit every plant in them.
Ensure real drainage — holes, and raised off the ground on feet.
Water far more often than you would ground-grown plants: daily in hot weather, sometimes twice.
Feed regularly, because container compost runs out of nutrients within about six weeks.
Practise succession sowing — a short row of salad every fortnight rather than all at once.
tips: Compost that has shrunk away from the pot edge lets water run straight down the sides. Soak the pot fully to rewet it.
Dark pots in full sun cook roots. Group pots together to shade each other.
proof: You harvest several different crops from containers across one season.
